label: positive
summary: ERC20 TREASURY MIGRATION - the gap 10.7 left open after the native-only pass. `feeRecipient` is established one-shot by the constructor at N-1 with no unguarded run-time writer; at N the constructor is gone and an unguarded external `init` sets it. It qualifies as value-holding because it is argument 0 of an ERC20 `transfer(to, amount)` - the most common real-world treasury shape, and the one native Transfer/Send detection cannot see. EXPECTED: quiet before the ERC20 widening, fires after.

label: negative
summary: APPROVE IS NOT A PAYMENT. Structurally identical migration, but `router` is only ever passed to `approve(spender, amount)`. An allowance grant names a SPENDER, not a destination - no value moves to it - and approving a DEX router is routine. This is the FP risk that native-only detection never had: match on 'address passed to an ERC20 call' and a router approval becomes indistinguishable from a treasury rotation. EXPECTED: quiet.

label: negative
summary: ARGUMENT POSITION MATTERS. `payer` is argument 0 of `transferFrom(from, to, amount)` - the SOURCE, not the recipient. Value moves AWAY from it. Taking position 0 as the destination for every ERC20 call would mark the payer as value-holding and fire here; the recipient of transferFrom is argument 1. EXPECTED: quiet.
